 Preview Lyon Open Final | Lorenzo Musetti aims to end seven-final losing streak against Taylor Fritz
 Originally posted on
 TennisUpToDate.com 
  | 
 Last updated Oct 24, 2026 8:35 PM ET
 Add us as a preferred source on Google
 Lorenzo Musetti and Taylor Fritz will meet in Sunday's final of the 2026 Lyon Open , with the Italian attempting to end a run of seven consecutive defeats in ATP Tour finals. Musetti earned his place in the championship match by saving four match points against compatriot Flavio Cobolli, winning 4-6, 6-2, 7-5 in a dramatic semifinal. Fritz, meanwhile, defeated Tommy Paul 6-3, 7-5, producing a dominant serving display to reach his fifth tour-level final of the season. 
 The ATP 250 event, played on indoor hard courts, has provided Musetti with an opportunity to rebuild his momentum after an injury-disrupted season. Fritz arrives with greater consistency in finals and a game suited to the conditions, although their head-to-head record gives the Italian a narrow 4-3 advantage. The match therefore brings together two contrasting storylines: Musetti's attempt to overcome his recent difficulties in championship matches and Fritz's pursuit of another title in a season in which he has already won in Washington. 
 Lorenzo Musetti seeks first title since 2022 after remarkable comeback
 Musetti enters the final ranked No. 26 in the live rankings, well below the career-high No. 5 he reached earlier in 2026. The Italian has won two ATP Tour titles, both in 2022, when he defeated Carlos Alcaraz in Hamburg and Matteo Berrettini in Naples. Since then, he has reached seven further finals without winning a trophy, including at Queen's Club, Umag, Chengdu (twice), Monte-Carlo, Athens and Hong Kong. 
 His run in Lyon has been one of the most demanding of the tournament. Musetti opened with a 6-1, 6-4 victory over Matteo Arnaldi before defeating French wildcard Moise Kouame 6-4, 6-4. In the quarterfinals, he survived a three-set battle against Luca Van Assche, winning 7-6 (5), 6-7 (7), 6-4 in a match that extended late into Friday night. That victory marked the 200th tour-level win of his career, adding a personal milestone to his progress through the draw. 
 The semifinal against top seed Cobolli required another level of resilience. After losing the opening set 6-4, Musetti responded by taking the second 6-2. He then faced four match points while serving at 4-5 in the deciding set, including two consecutive chances from 15/40. He saved all four before breaking Cobolli and completing a 4-6, 6-2, 7-5 victory after two hours and 32 minutes. 
 That comeback gives Musetti confidence heading into the final, but the physical demands of his last two matches cannot be ignored. He has played two consecutive three-set contests, including a quarterfinal that finished after 1 a.m. His recovery time could be important against Fritz, who reached the final in straight sets in both of his last two matches.

 The most significant statistic hanging over Musetti is his record in finals. His last title came in Naples in November 2022, and he has lost every final he has contested since then. His most recent disappointment came in Hong Kong in January, when Alexander Bublik defeated him 7-6 (2), 6-3. Lyon gives him a chance to end that streak, but doing so will require him to maintain the level he showed when saving match points against Cobolli.

 Musetti's all-court game offers several ways to challenge Fritz. The Italian can vary the height and pace of his groundstrokes, use his one-handed backhand to change direction and bring opponents forward with drop shots. On indoor hard courts, however, he will have less time to construct points against Fritz's serve and aggressive first shot. His ability to return effectively and avoid being pushed too far behind the baseline could determine whether he gets enough opportunities to break. 
 Taylor Fritz targets another title after serving masterclass against Paul
 Fritz arrives in the final ranked No. 14 in the live rankings and seeking to add another trophy to his 2026 campaign. The American won the Washington title earlier this season and has reached several other finals, including in Dallas, Stuttgart and Halle. Lyon represents his fifth tour-level final of the year and the 24th of his career, giving him another opportunity to build on an already consistent record at the highest level. 
 The second seed has looked increasingly comfortable as the week has progressed. He opened with a 6-2, 7-5 victory over Pierre-Hugues Herbert before beating Daniel Altmaier 7-6 (5), 6-2 in the quarterfinals. His semifinal against Paul was his strongest serving performance of the week, with 15 aces and all nine break points saved. Fritz won 6-3, 7-5 without allowing his opponent to convert a single break-point opportunity. 
 Fritz's serving numbers are particularly relevant to the final. His first serve can generate free points, while his ability to dictate the next shot makes him difficult to contain on an indoor hard court. Against Paul, he also demonstrated his composure under pressure, saving three set points in one game before taking control of the match. That combination of serving power and efficiency could prove decisive against Musetti, who has spent considerably more time on court during the latter stages of the tournament. 
 The American's season has nevertheless included setbacks in finals. Although he captured the Washington title, he has also finished runner-up in other championship matches this year. Lyon would provide an opportunity to add another title and reinforce his position heading into the final stretch of the season. Unlike Musetti, however, Fritz is not carrying a seven-final losing streak into the contest, and his recent results suggest he is comfortable managing the demands of a championship match.

 Fritz's route to the final has been notably more straightforward than Musetti's. He has won all three matches in straight sets, while the Italian has played two consecutive deciding sets and saved four match points in his semifinal. That difference could become increasingly important if the final develops into a long contest. 
 The tactical challenge for Fritz will be to prevent Musetti from disrupting his rhythm. The Italian's variety can force opponents to generate their own pace, but Fritz will want to shorten rallies and avoid allowing Musetti to dictate with changes of height and direction. If the American maintains his serving efficiency, he could put sustained pressure on Musetti's service games.

 Head-to-head: Musetti leads Fritz 4-3
 Musetti leads the Head2Head 4-3, including a straight-sets victory in their most recent meeting at the Australian Open in January. The Italian won that fourth-round encounter 6-2, 7-5, 6-4, showing that he can neutralize Fritz's power and establish control from the baseline. Their previous meetings give Musetti a narrow statistical advantage, although the indoor conditions in Lyon present a different challenge. 
 The final presents a clear contrast in playing styles and recent form. Musetti has shown that he can survive difficult situations and compete under pressure, but he must recover physically and find ways to prevent Fritz from dominating with his serve. Fritz, meanwhile, will look to exploit the indoor conditions, keep points short and make Musetti work hard to earn every break opportunity. 
 For Musetti, the stakes extend beyond another tournament title. Ending his seven-final losing streak would remove a persistent obstacle from his recent career and reward a week in which he has repeatedly recovered from difficult positions. For Fritz, the objective is more straightforward: convert his strong serving form and efficient route through the draw into another trophy.
